format: errante-compare/0 (provisional; not part of the data contract)
method: Per detector: weighted coadd of the field's frames in each season (one weight per frame from its background variance; sky removed; bad and display-repaired pixels excluded). Difference = later - s * earlier, with s the sigma-clipped median of field-star aperture ratios, each star measured above its local sky ring (4-7 px), outside a circle around the target at the field centre of 1.2 x its halo radius in the earlier coadd (8 px minimum, 45% of the grid size maximum). This cancels the wavelength change between exposures for typical field stars. Units MJy/sr (IMAGE - ZODI). A moving star appears as an orange/cyan dipole; static stars cancel.
limitations: Each coadd uses only the field's selected frames (a few per season and detector); they sample different wavelengths in each season. A same-sign residual on a star whose colour differs from the field stars (e.g. a red dwarf) is not evidence of variability unless the wavelengths are matched.

The flux scale is fitted on field stars (each above its local sky ring) outside a circle around the field centre that grows with the target's halo (up to 45% of the grid size); with fewer than 5 usable stars s = 1 and the difference also shows the wavelength change. A saturated target in a sparse field (e.g. R Draconis) often leaves too few stars and falls back to s = 1.
Saturated cores and detector defects carry no valid data (grey checkerboard).

Display only: the colour range is the field's brightest residuals or 10 x the noise (noise = robust sigma of the difference image). When the target region is much fainter (field range >= 2 x target-region range, e.g. WISE 0855), the range is set from the target region (its second-largest residual: one hot pixel cannot set it, and the brightest pixel there may clip) and brighter field-star residuals clip (saturate). Residuals under ~3 x the noise stay dark.
With two or three frames per season and detector, a faint target can stay in the noise: an empty target region at this depth is not evidence that the target did not move or vary.
weights_definition: Per coadd, 'weights' lists one weight per frame in the order of 'frame_ids': 1 / median VARIANCE of the frame's usable pixels, in (MJy/sr)^-2 (1 / robust noise^2 for a frame without a VARIANCE plane). Each pixel is the weighted mean of the frames valid there (sky removed per frame).
display: Signed asinh: v = asinh(x / (softening x limit)) / asinh(1 / softening) for a residual x (MJy/sr) clipped at +/- limit ('limit_mjy_sr'). softening = min(1, max(0.05, 3 x noise / limit)) ('display_softening'), where noise is the robust sigma (1.4826 x median absolute deviation) of the difference image's valid pixels (not 'noise_mjy_sr', which comes from the propagated VARIANCE). 'field_limit_mjy_sr' = 99.9th percentile of the field's |residuals| or 10 x noise, whichever is larger. 'target_limit_mjy_sr' = second-largest |residual| within 'target_exclude_px' of the field centre (so one hot pixel or cosmic ray cannot set it; the brightest pixel there may clip), at least 10 x noise. 'limit_rule' is 'target_region' (limit = target limit) when the field limit is >= 2 x the target limit, else 'field' (limit = field limit).

colors.positive: orange: brighter in the later season
colors.negative: cyan: brighter in the earlier season
colors.no_data: grey checkerboard: no valid data (off the cutout or saturated core)

notes: Target core flagged: pixels within 2 px of the field centre are flagged or invalid in at least one frame of the coadd (D1_S1: 1 of 12 px). Those pixels average fewer frames (other wavelengths) or, when flagged in every frame, have no data (grey checkerboard), so the difference there is not a clean brightness measurement.

Faint target: display limit set from the target region (0.115 MJy/sr, 10 x the noise: the second-largest residual within 8 px of the field centre is fainter than that) instead of the field (1.06 MJy/sr); field-star residuals clip.
